correctness.rationale: The block-incidence graph is a tree, so every nonroot vertex has a unique previous-layer neighbour, and its same-layer neighbours form exactly one forward clique. Stable colouring determines distances, clique colour signatures, and clique multiplicities. Descending reconstruction of rooted descendant graphs and ascending automorphism induction prove orbit exactness, including arbitrary initial precolours. All boundary cases covered; two independent finite checkers corroborate the structural statements.

originality.rationale: The main claim is an infinite, arbitrary-marked connected-block-graph orbit classification. The closest examined works give the general refinability framework, rooted-tree cases, identification criteria and a general individualization hierarchy, not this projected clique-tree theorem. Keyword and semantic searches found no equivalent or stronger block-graph statement. Specialized earlier literature remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: A universal orbit-exactness theorem for rooted block graphs is a natural structural milestone: all clique sizes, block-tree shapes, root choices and additional colours are admitted, whereas the unmarked property fails. The proof gives a constructive way to decode hidden block information from ordinary counting signatures. It provides a useful all-order logical invariant rather than a narrow numerical lookup.
